name: Serapeum of Alexandria
text: The Serapeum of Alexandria was an ancient Greek temple built by Ptolemy III Euergetes and dedicated to the Greco-Egyptian syncretic god Serapis, who was believed to be the protector of Alexandria, Egypt. It was built during the 3rd century BCE, primarily  between 246 and 222 BCE. It housed the daughter library of Alexandria.

depictions.name: Serapeum of Alexandria
depictions.text: The Serapeum of Alexandria was an ancient Greek temple located in Alexandria, Egypt, dedicated to Serapis, the patron god of the city. Considered to be the most beautiful place in Alexandria, it was located southwest of the city on a small hill known as the Acropolis. Its foundations were created during the reign of pharaoh Ptolemy I Soter, and the temple was finished during the reign of Ptolemy III.
